parsed.main_gap: Step 2 justifies 'some entry >1 always remains' with the false principle that a non-increasing positive integer starting above 1 never reaches 1; the correct reason (a move never creates two 1's) appears only in the summary.

errors.description: The key lemma of part (a) — that the board never becomes all 1's — is justified by a false general principle: a non-increasing sequence of positive integers starting above 1 certainly can reach 1 (e.g. P: 4→2→1). The valid argument (g and ℓ cannot both equal 1, so the count of entries >1 drops by at most one per move) is stated only in the 'Current best' summary, not in the formal proof.
errors.quote:
A positive integer that never increases and starts above 1 can never reach 1; hence
$P > 1$ after any number of moves.

parsed.notes: Termination bound, prime-wise gcd-of-valuations invariant, and terminal evaluation are all correct and cleanly written. Only the 'not all ones' step is mis-justified, and it is repairable in one line using a fact the author already states elsewhere.
